book_title:
The Second Epistle of Paul
to Timothee.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE SECOND EPISTLE OF S. PAUL TO TIMOTHEE.
intros.text:
THE chief scope of this second to Timothee, is, to open unto him that his martyrdom is at hand. Which yet he doth not plainly before the end: preparing first his mind with much circumstance, because he knew it would grieve him sore, and also might be a tentation unto him. Therefore he talketh of the cause of his trouble, & of the reward: that the one is honourable, and the other most glorious: and exhorteth him to be constant in the faith, to be ready always to suffer for it, to fulfill his ministry to the end, as himself now had done his.
Whereby it is certain, that it was written at Rome, in his last apprehension and imprisonment there: as he signifieth by these words Cap. 1: Onesiphorus was not ashamed of my chain, but when he was come to Rome, carefully sought me, &c. And of his martyrdom, thus: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my resolution (or death) is at hand. cap. 4.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> an Apostle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ by the vvil of God, according to the promisse of the life vvhich is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>:
to Timothee my deerest sonne, grace, mercie, peace from God the father, and Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord.
I giue thankes to God, vvhom I serue from my progenitours in a pure conscience, that vvithout intermission I haue a memorie of thee in my praiers, night and day
desiring to see thee, mindeful of thy teares, that I may be filled vvith ioy,
calling to minde that faith vvhich is in thee not feined, vvhich also dvvelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice, and I am sure that in thee also.
For the vvhich cause I admonish thee that thou resuscitate the <na>[1]</na> grace of God, vvhich is in thee by the imposition of my handes.

notes.text: Here againe it is plaine that holy Orders giue grace, & that euen by and in the external ceremonie of imposing the Bishops hands. And it is a maner of speach specially vsed in this Apostle and S. Luke, that Orders giue grace to the ordered, & that to take orders or authoritie to minister Sacramēts or preach, is, to be giuen or deliuered to Gods grace. Act. 14, 25.

verses.text: For God hath not giuen vs the spirit of feare: but of povver, and loue, and sobrietie.
Be not therfore ashamed of the testimonie of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but trauail vvith the Gospel according to the povver of God,

vvho hath deliuered and called vs by his holy calling, <cr>[1]</cr> not according to our vvorkes, but according to his purpose and grace, vvhich vvas giuen to vs in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> <cr>[2]</cr> before the secular times.
But it is manifested novv by the illumination of our Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, vvho hath destroied death, & illuminated life and incorruption by the Gospel:
vvherein <cr>[1]</cr> I am appointed a preacher and Apostle and Maister of the Gentiles.
For the vvhich cause also I suffer these things: but I am not cõfounded. For I knovv vvhom I haue beleeued, & I am sure that he is able to keepe my depositum vnto that day.
Haue thou a forme of sound vvordes, vvhich thou hast heard of me in faith & <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> in the loue in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: c Faith and love coupled commonly together in this Apostle's writings.

verses.text: Keepe the good depositum by the holy Ghost, vvhich dvvelleth in vs.
Thou knovvest this, that al vvhich are in Asia, be auerted from me: of vvhom is Phigelus and Hermogenes.
Our Lord giue mercie to <cr>[1]</cr> the house of Onesiphorus: because he hath often refreshed me, and hath <na>[2]</na> not been ashamed of my chaine.

notes.text: What a happy and meritorious thing it is to relieve the afflicted for religion, and not to be ashamed of their disgrace, irons or what miseries soever. · 2 Timothy 4:19.

verses.text: but vvhen he vvas come to Rome: he sought me carefully, and found me.
Our Lord graunt him to finde mercie of our Lord in that day. And how many things he ministred to me at Ephesus, thou knovvest better.

chapters.summary: Vvith his praises he couertly exhorteth him not to be dismaied for his trouble, 6 (hauing grace giuen in Orders to helpe him, 8 and knovving for vvhat cause he is persecuted) and namely vvith the example of Onesiphorus.

verses.text: <sc>THOV</sc> therfore my sonne, be strong in the grace vvhich is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>:
& the things vvhich thou hast heard of me by many vvitnesses, these cōmend to faithful men, vvhich shal be fit to teach others also.
Labour thou as a good souldiar of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
No man being a souldiar to God, intãgleth him self vvith secular businesses: that he may please him to vvhom he hath approued him self.
For he also that striueth for the maisterie, is not crovvned vnlesse he striue lavvfully.
The husbandman that laboureth, must first take of the fruites.
Vnderstand vvhat I say: for our Lord vvil giue thee in al things vnderstanding.
<na>[1]</na> Be mindeful that our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ is risen againe from the dead, of the seede of Dauid, according to my Gospel,

notes.text: b Part of the Epistle upon S. George's day. April. 25. The rest is pa. 541.

verses.text: vvherein I labour euen vnto bandes, as a malefactour: but the vvord of God is not tied.
Therfore <na>[1]</na> I sustaine al things for the elect, that they also may obtaine the saluation, vvhich is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, vvith heauenly glorie.

notes.text: Marke here that the elect (though sure of saluation) yet are saued by meanes of their preachers & teachers, as also by their owne endeuours.

verses.text: A faithful saying. For if vve be dead vvith him, vve shal liue also together.
If vve shal sustaine, vve shal also reigne together. <cr>[1]</cr> If vve shal deny, he also vvil denie vs.
<cr>[1]</cr> If vve beleeue not: he continueth faithful, he can not denie him self.
These things admonish: testifying before our Lord. Contend not in vvordes, for it is profitable for nothing, but for the subuersion of them that heare.
Carefully prouide to present thy self approued to God, a vvorkeman not to be confounded, rightly handling the vvord of truth.
But <na>[1]</na> cprofane and vaine speaches auoid: for they doe much grovv to impietie:

notes.text: c See the Annotations before 1. Tim. 6. v. 20.

verses.text: & their speache spreadeth as a canker: of vvhom is Hymenæus and Philetus:
vvho haue erred from the truth, saying that the resurrection is done already, and haue subuerted the faith of some.
But the sure foundation of God standeth, hauing this seale, Our Lord knovveth, vvho be his, and let euery one depart from iniquitie that nameth the name of our Lord.
But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of siluer, but also of vvood and of earth: and certaine in deede vnto honour, but certaine vnto contumelie.
If any man therfore shal cleanse him self from these, he shal be a vessel vnto honour, sanctified & profitable to our Lord, prepared to euery good vvorke.
But youthful desires flee: and pursue iustice, faith, charitie, & peace vvith them that inuocate our Lord from a pure hart.
And <cr>[1]</cr> foolish and vnlearned questiõs auoid, knovving that they ingender braules.
But the seruant of our Lord must not vvrangle: but be milde tovvard al men, apt to teache, patient,
vvith modestie admonishing them that resist the truth: lest sometime <na>[1]</na> God giue them repentance to knovv the truth:

notes.text: Conuersion from sinne and heresie is the gift of God and of his special grace: yet here vve see, good exhortations and praier and such other helpes of man be profitable therevnto. Vvhich could not be, if vve had not free vvill.

verses.text: and they recouer them selues from the snares of the deuil, of vvhom they are held captiue at his vvil.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth him to labour diligently in his office, considering the revvard in Christ, and his denial of them that deny him. 14 Not to contend, but to shunne heretikes: neither to be moued to see some subuerted, considering that the elect continue Catholikes, and that in the Church be of al sortes. 24 Yet vvith al svveetenes to reclaime the deceiued.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> this knovv thou, that <cr>[1]</cr> in the last daies shal approche perilous times.
and men shal be louers of them selues, couetous, hautie, proud, blasphemous, not obedient to their parents, vnkinde, vvicked,
vvithout affection, vvithout peace, accusers, incontinent, vnmerciful, vvithout benignitie,
traitours, stubburne, puffed vp, and louers of voluptuousnes more then of God:
hauing an appearance in deede of pietie, but denying the vertue thereof. And these auoid.
For of these be they that craftely enter into houses: and leade captiue seely vvomen loden vvith sinnes, vvhich are ledde vvith diuers desires:
alvvaies learning, and neuer attaining to the knovvledge of the truth.
But as <cr>[1]</cr> Iannes & Mambres <na>[2]</na> resisted Moyses, so these also resist the truth, men corrupted in minde, reprobate cõcerning the faith.

notes.text: Exo. 7. · ∷That those Magicians vvhich resisted Moyses, vvere thus called, it is not vvritten in al the old Testament. therfore it came to the Apostles knovvledge by tradition, as the Church novv hath the names of the 3 kings, of the penitent theefe, of the souldiar that pearced Christes side on the Crosse, and of the like.

verses.text: But they shal prosper no further: for their folly shal be manifest to al, as theirs also vvas.
<na>[1]</na> But thou hast attained to my doctrine, institution, purpose, faith, longanimitie, loue, patience,

notes.text: b The rest of the Epist. for S. George's day.

verses.text: persecutions, passions: vvhat maner of things vvere done to me at Antioche, at Iconium, at Lystra: vvhat maner of persecutiõs I sustained. and out of al our Lord deliuered me.
And al that vvil liue godly in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, shal suffer persecution.
But euil men and seducers shal prosper to the vvorse: erring, and driuing into errour.
But thou, <na>[1]</na> continue in those things vvhich thou hast learned, and are committed to thee: knovving of vvhom thou hast learned:

notes.text: ∷In al danger and diuersitie of false sectes, S. Paules admonition is, euer to abide in that vvas first taught & deliuered, neuer to giue ouer our old faith for a new fansie. This is it vvhich before he calleth depositum. 1. Tim. 6. and 2. Tim. 1.

verses.text: and because from thine infancie thou hast knovven the holy Scriptures, vvhich can instruct thee to saluation, by the faith that is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
<cr>[1]</cr> All Scripture inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to argue, to correct, to instruct in iustice:
that the man of God may be perfect, instructed to euery good vvorke.

chapters.summary: He prophecieth of Heretikes to come, 6 and noteth certaine then also for such, bidding him to auoid them, 10 and (vvhat so euer persecution befall for it) to cõtinue constant in the Catholike doctrine, both because of his Maister (S. Paul him self) 15 and also because of his ovvne knovvledge in the Scriptures.

verses.text: I <na>[1]</na> Testifie before God and <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ vvho shal iudge the liuing and the dead, and by his aduent, and his kingdom:

notes.text: The Epistle for holy Doctors, and for S. Silvester. Decemb. 31. & for S. Hilary, Ian. 14. and S. Dominic August 4.

verses.text: Preach the vvord. vrge in season, out of season, reproue, beseeche, rebuke in al patience and doctrine.
For there shal be a time vvhen they vvil not beare sound doctrine: but according to their ovvne desires they vvil heape to them selues maisters, hauing itching eares,
and from the truth certes they vvil auert their hearing, and to fables they vvil be conuerted.
But be thou vigilant, labour in al things, doe the vvorke of an Euangelist, fulfil thy ministerie. Be sober.
For I am euen novv <na>[1]</na> to be sacrificed: & the time of my resolutiõ is at hand.

notes.text: The martyrdom of saincts is so acceptable to God, that it is counted as it vvere a sacrifice in his sight, and therfore hath many effectes both in the partie that suffereth it, and in others that are partakers of the merite as of a sacrifice: vvhich name it hath by a Metaphore.

verses.text: I haue fought a good fight, I haue consummate my course, I haue kept the faith.
Concerning the rest, there is laid vp for me a crovvne of iustice, vvhich our Lord vvil render to me in that day, a iust iudge: and not only to me, but to them also that loue his comming. ⊢
Make hast to come to me quickly.
For Demas hath left me, louing this vvorld, and is gone to Thessalonica: Crescens into Galatia, Titus into Dalmatia.
<cr>[1]</cr> Luke only is vvith me. Take Marke, and bring him vvith thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministerie.
But Tychicus I haue sent to Ephesus.
The cloke that I left at Troas vvith Carpus, cõming bring vvith thee, and the bookes, especially the parchement.
Alexander the Coppersmith hath shevved me much euil, our Lord vvil revvard him according to his vvorkes:
vvhom doe thou also auoid, for he hath greatly resisted our vvordes.
In my first ansvver no man vvas vvith me, but al did forsake me: be it not imputed to them.
But our Lord stoode to me, and strengthened me, that by me the preaching may be accomplished, and al Gentiles may heare: and I vvas deliuered from the mouth of the lion.
Our Lord <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘hath deliuered</alt>’ me from al euil vvorke: and vvil saue me vnto his heauenly kingdom. to vvhom be glorie for euer & euer. Amen.
Salute Prisca and Aquila, and <cr>[1]</cr> the house of Onesiphorus.
Erastus remained at Corinth. And Trophimus I left sicke at Miletum.
Make hast to come before vvinter. Eubulus and Pudens and <na>[1]</na> Linus and Claudia, and al the brethren, salute thee.

notes.text: ᶜThis Linus vvas coadiutor vvith & vnder S. Peter, & so counted secõd in the number of Popes.

verses.text: Our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ be vvith thy spirit. Grace be vvith you. Amen.

chapters.summary: He requireth him to be earnest vvhile he may, because the time vvil come vvhen they vvil not abide Catholike preaching, 5 and to fulfil his course, as him self novv hath done. 9 and to come vnto him vvith speede, because the rest of his traine are dispersed, and he dravveth novv to heauen.
